issue_title: bug(io): Zemax import ignores UNIT INCH and reads inches as millimetres
issue_body:
## Summary

`ZemaxSystemImporter._parse_surfaces()` reads only `SURF` blocks and ignores header keywords. A file declaring `UNIT INCH` is interpreted 1:1 as millimetres, so every radius, thickness, diameter, and gap is 25.4× too small.

## Impact

- Importing an inch-based `.zmx` silently produces a completely different optical system (25.4× scale error) instead of converting or refusing.
- The importer's docstring explicitly claims tolerant handling of foreign sequential files.
- Downstream focal lengths, f-numbers, and tolerances are all wrong by the same factor.

## Reproduction

```text
header: UNIT INCH; thickness 1.0 in = 25.4 mm; DIAM 0.5 in = 12.7 mm semi
imported thickness: 1.0 mm   (expected 25.4)
imported diameter:  1.0 mm   (expected 25.4)
imported radius 1:  25.400000025908 mm (expected 25.4 in = 645.16)
imported air gap:   4.0 mm   (expected 4 in = 101.6)
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/export_formats.py:967-982` — `import_system` rebuilds from parsed surfaces; no unit handling.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:816-817` — parser only recognizes `SURF` lines.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:1031` — `diam * 2.0` is assumed to be mm.

## Expected behaviour

`UNIT INCH`/`UNIT MM` is honoured: every parsed length is converted to mm once, at the parse boundary. Unknown units raise or warn instead of silently assuming mm.

## Suggested fix

Parse the header for `UNIT` (Zemax also uses `UNIT INCH`, `UNIT MM`, and older `MM`/`IN` markers), store a scale factor, and apply it to `CURV` (inverse), `DISZ`, `DIAM`, and thickness/gap values. Add a test with an inch file asserting the converted geometry.
pr_title: fix(io): convert Zemax inch files to millimetres
pr_body:
## Description

`ZemaxSystemImporter._parse_surfaces()` read only `SURF` blocks and ignored
the header, so a file declaring `UNIT INCH` was interpreted 1:1 as
millimetres. Every radius, thickness, aperture and gap came out 25.4x too
small, and the import still reported success:

```text
header: UNIT INCH; thickness 1.0 in = 25.4 mm; DIAM 0.5 in = 12.7 mm semi
imported thickness: 1.0 mm   (expected 25.4)
imported diameter:  1.0 mm   (expected 25.4)
imported radius 1:  25.400000025908 mm (expected 25.4 in = 645.16)
imported air gap:   4.0 mm   (expected 4 in = 101.6)
```

Downstream focal lengths, f-numbers and tolerances were all wrong by the same
factor, with nothing in the file or the UI saying so.

## What changed

- **`openlens/export_formats.py`** - a new `_parse_unit_scale()` reads the
  `UNIT` header. `MM` (and the spelled-out millimetre forms) maps to 1.0,
  `IN`/`INCH`/`INCHES` maps to 25.4. A file with no `UNIT` line keeps the
  historical millimetre default, as Zemax does; an explicit unknown unit logs
  a warning and also uses millimetres rather than aborting the import.
- `import_system()` normalises the parsed values to millimetres once: `DISZ`
  and `DIAM` multiply by the factor, `CURV` divides by it (curvature is the
  inverse of a length). Non-finite marker values (`DISZ INFINITY`) pass
  through untouched, and every consumer below stays unit-agnostic.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #626

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Six new tests in `tests/test_zemax_roundtrip.py::TestZemaxUnits`. Four fail on
the unfixed code:

- `test_inch_lengths_are_converted_to_millimetres` - radii 50.8 mm,
  thicknesses 25.4/12.7 mm, diameters 12.7/25.4 mm
- `test_the_gap_between_elements_is_converted` - the 4 in gap is 101.6 mm
- `test_the_inch_spellings_are_recognised` - `UNIT INCH`, `UNIT IN`,
  `unit inch`
- `test_unknown_unit_warns_and_assumes_millimetres`

Two guard the existing behaviour:

- `test_a_millimetre_file_is_unchanged`
- `test_a_missing_unit_line_keeps_millimetres`

The Zemax round-trip, export-format, export-service and import-limit suites
(64 tests) pass after rebasing onto current `master`; full local suite on the
pre-rebase tree: `Ran 2753 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`.
